rows.text: August 11, 2005
The Monetary Policy Committee of the Bank of Korea decided today to maintain the benchmark call rate (uncollateralized overnight rate) at its current level (3.25%) for the intermeeting period.
(An unofficial English translation based on the Korean original of the decision on monetary policy taken by the Monetary Policy Committee on August 11, 2005 is attached.)
The Bank of Korea
Monetary Policy Decision
In the real economy, while exports continue to exhibit steady growth, private consumption shows more apparent signs of recovery and construction investment maintains a growing pace.
On the other hand, an improvement of facilities investment has not yet become evident.
The Monetary Policy Committee of the Bank of Korea decided today to maintain the benchmark call rate (uncollateralized overnight rate) at its current level (3.25%) for the intermeeting period.
(An unofficial English translation based on the Korean original of the decision on monetary policy taken by the Monetary Policy Committee on August 11, 2005 is attached.)
Meanwhile, the current account is still running a surplus, thanks to that on the goods account.
Despite the persistence of high oil prices, both consumer price inflation and core inflation continue to exhibit overall stability as upward pressure from the demand side has been subdued.
In the real economy, while exports continue to exhibit steady growth, private consumption shows more apparent signs of recovery and construction investment maintains a growing pace.
On the other hand, an improvement of facilities investment has not yet become evident.
Real estate prices, centering on house prices, have exhibited a slowdown in their upward pace ahead of the government's announcement of a comprehensive package of stabilization measures.

In the financial markets, while overall liquidity conditions are favorable and financial institutions' loans are still increasing steadily, long-term market interest rates have shown a relatively sharp increase.
Meanwhile, the current account is still running a surplus, thanks to that on the goods account.

Taking the above economic and financial conditions into consideration, the Monetary Policy Committee of the Bank of Korea decided today to maintain the benchmark call rate (uncollateralized overnight rate) at its current level (3.25 percent) for the intermeeting period.
